hints: Expand the top value as XORs of bottom-row values.
A bottom value appears according to a binomial coefficient modulo two.
Coefficient C(n-1,i) is odd exactly when i uses only bits present in n-1.
analogy: Repeated XOR forms Pascal's triangle with even counts cancelling out.
example: For bottom row [1,2,3], the top is (1 XOR 2) XOR (2 XOR 3)=1 XOR 3=2.
algorithm: For every zero-based index i from 0 through n-1, XOR a[i] into the answer if (i AND (n-1)) equals i. Print the result.
correctness: After n-1 levels, a[i] appears C(n-1,i) times. XOR keeps it only when that coefficient is odd; Lucas' theorem gives the stated bit-subset test.
complexity: For n bottom values, O(n) time and O(1) extra space.
